c: Transfers, shared care and Right to Choose
A handover is only complete when the receiving prescriber has accepted it. Until then, ask who prescribes.
(discharge without a receiving prescriber). In each case the safe default is the same: the current prescriber stays responsible until the next one has accepted.
Ministers have said GP practices may decline ADHD shared care, and that responsibility then stays with the specialist.
GP practices may decline shared care for capacity or confidence reasons, especially with independent providers.
Local commissioning policies change, and old rules can be quoted after they have been replaced.

In Coventry and Warwickshire, the commissioner's 2025 ADHD referral policy (COM/46) stated that patients already on the waiting list or under follow-up would be funded; project records indicate it was replaced by an all-age policy from 14 May 2026, whose text should be obtained before relying on either.
Ask any new provider, in writing:
Will you prescribe directly until a shared-care agreement is accepted?
What records do you need from the previous service, and will you request them?
What is your restart plan and review schedule?
Who do I contact between appointments?
